# NeuralNg Input

> Native Angular 22+ text input enhancement at `@neural-ng/core/input`.

## Rules

- Import `NeuralInput` from `@neural-ng/core/input` and add it to standalone
  component imports.
- Generate `<input neuralInput>`, not `<neural-input>` and not a wrapper div.
- Keep native attributes such as `type`, `name`, `autocomplete`, `required`,
  `disabled`, `readonly`, `minlength`, and `maxlength` on the input.
- Use Input for text-like types: text, email, password, search, tel, and url.
- Do not use this primitive to style checkbox, radio, range, color, file,
  date/time, or numeric interaction models.
- Use a native `<label for>` or another valid accessible name. Placeholder text
  is not a label.
- Associate help and error content through `aria-describedby`.
- Apply `aria-invalid="true"` only when a validation error exists and provide a
  human-readable correction message.
- For Angular Signal Forms, import `FormField` from `@angular/forms/signals`
  and bind `[formField]` directly to the same native input.
- For template-driven Forms, import `FormsModule` and use `[(ngModel)]` on the
  native input. Keep `name` when the input participates in a form.
- For Reactive Forms, import `ReactiveFormsModule` and use `[formControl]` or
  `formControlName` directly on the native input.
- Signal Forms exposes invalid/touched state; explicitly bind `aria-invalid`
  and connect the rendered error message with `aria-describedby`.
- When Input is inside `neural-field`, let Field supply its ID, ARIA
  relationships, state, fluid width, and inherited unstyled mode.
- Do not create a ControlValueAccessor for this component; its host is already
  a native form control.
- Use the normal `class` or `[class.*]` APIs directly. There is no `inputClass`
  input because no internal input element exists.
- Use `inputSize="small|medium|large"` for visual sizing. Do not replace the
  native HTML `size` attribute; both APIs can coexist.
- Use `variant="outlined|filled"` for the visual treatment. The default is
  `outlined`.
- `fluid` applies full width only in styled mode.
- `unstyled` removes visual and fluid classes while preserving the structural
  hook and all native behavior.
- For logical start/end icons, import `NeuralInputGroup` and compose
  `<neural-input-group startIcon="nt nt-search"><input neuralInput /></neural-input-group>`.
  Keep the accessible name on the native input; group icons are decorative.
- Do not invent clear, mask, or password-toggle inputs on this primitive.

## Canonical example

```ts
import { FormField, email, form, required } from '@angular/forms/signals';
import { NeuralInput } from '@neural-ng/core/input';

readonly model = signal({ email: '' });
readonly accountForm = form(this.model, (path) => {
  required(path.email, { message: 'Email is required.' });
  email(path.email, { message: 'Enter a valid email address.' });
});
```

```html
<label for="account-email">Email</label>
<input
  neuralInput
  fluid
  id="account-email"
  name="email"
  type="email"
  autocomplete="email"
  [formField]="accountForm.email"
  [attr.aria-invalid]="
    accountForm.email().touched() && accountForm.email().invalid()
      ? 'true'
      : null
  "
/>
```

The rendered control is the original native input. Preserve that semantic and
form behavior when generating surrounding layout or validation UI.
